ground_truth.description: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.root_cause: Factory.deploy uses create2 but reverts with CreateCollision if address exists, violating ERC-4337 expectation to return address. Breaks simulations and bundler logic.
ground_truth.attack_scenario: Deploy wallet once, call deploy again → reverts. Attacker can front-run to cause DoS. PoC: test_factory_double_deploy_PoC in AuditPoC.sol. Shows first deploy succeeds, second reverts.
ground_truth.fix_description: Check if address exists via predicted.code.length, return it if so.

vulnerabilities.explanation: The deploy function uses CREATE2 but reverts with DeployFailed error when the target address already exists (contract == address(0)). This violates ERC-4337 expectations where factories should return the existing address instead of reverting. This breaks bundler logic and simulations.
vulnerabilities.attack_scenario: 1. Deploy a wallet once via Factory.deploy. 2. Call deploy again with same parameters - transaction reverts. 3. An attacker can front-run legitimate deployments to cause collisions, making legitimate deployments fail.
vulnerabilities.suggested_fix: Check if contract exists via predicted.code.length before CREATE2. If exists, return the address. Example fix: bytes32 predicted = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(type(Wallet).creationCode, uint256(uint160(_mainModule)), _salt)); if (predicted.code.length > 0) return predicted; else proceed with CREATE2.

prediction.overall_explanation: The Factory contract has a clear vulnerability where it fails to handle CREATE2 collisions properly. Instead of returning the existing address when a wallet already exists at the predicted address, it reverts. This breaks ERC-4337 compliance and can be exploited for DoS attacks through front-running. The vulnerability is well-documented in the provided benchmark.
